Indexed recurrent KDA uses a state pool and a sequence-by-token index table to resume accepted states and publish per-token states. Three storage paths violate that contract: two-dimensional index views lose their token stride, indexed out-of-place output allocates one state per sequence, and indexed writes execute when both state outputs are disabled. items.title: [Bug]: registerCliBackend without modelProvider is silently dropped, and the failure surfaces as "Invalid URL: must be http or https"
items.body_excerpt:
### Summary

OpenClaw binds a model provider to a CLI runtime only when the registered CLI backend declares a `modelProvider` field. When the field is missing, `addCliRuntimeModelBinding` returns early without creating the binding and without emitting any diagnostic. items.body_excerpt:
Fixes #10962.

## Problem

`acquireTrustLockSync` retried an `ELOCKED` trust lock in a synchronous busy-wait on the wall clock:

```ts
const start = Date.now();
while (Date.now() - start < delayMs) { /* spin */ }
```

When a test freezes the clock (vitest fake timers), the loop can never terminate: the worker spins at 100% CPU forever, the designed ~200ms give-up-then-throw is never reached, and the worker ignores SIGINT while spinning. Reproduced and CDP-sampled in #10962 — the sampled worker's stack sat in `acquireTrustLockSync` with `Date.now()` returning the identical value across seconds.

Note the frozen clock makes this worse than ordinary contention: the spin never re-checks the lock

items.title: fix(ai): adapt OAuth device polling margin after slow_down
items.body_excerpt:
TL;DR: WSL / Ubuntu is stupid and can easily lead to persistently a bit too fast (10 %) clock. This, in turn, can make oauth requests to COPILOT just a bit faster than "slow-down", leading to it *never* succeeding. Layers of suck.

Obv. it should be fixed in Ubuntu wsl (https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntuwsl/+bug/2170230) or WSL2 (https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/12583) but until then, probably worth fixing it here given #1990, #6187 (some of those protections got removed). 

With this fix, we double the margin 2x on each subsequent slow down failure. That way we don't slow it down when we don't need to but do when we do. Might help other oauth other than copilot.
